title: Centralize Retry Jitter Config
readme_md:
# Centralize Retry Jitter Config

**Category:** Refactoring  
**Difficulty:** Easy  

## Scenario

A partner webhook retry storm hit the same downstream service every five seconds for half an hour. The retry settings live in more than one place, so two paths behaved differently during the outage. On-call wants the retry timing made consistent before the next partner launch. Keep the existing retry calls easy to use for small jobs.

## System Context

- The workflow crosses service boundaries where retries, duplicate delivery, and partial failure are normal.
- Operators rely on logs/metrics/audit events to replay incidents and verify recovery.
- Downstream consumers depend on stable response envelopes and event semantics.

## Your Task

- Centralize retry timing and jitter configuration used by webhook delivery.
- Preserve the public functions and returned payload keys.
- Keep the behavior runnable with Python 3.10+.

# soul.md prebake · Centralize Retry Jitter Config

## What this problem really tests

**Single source of truth for retry policy**: when retry timing and jitter live in two places (e.g., one in the webhook handler, one in the inner client), an outage that fires the inner path twice as often as the outer path is invisible until it hits production. The fix is to extract a single config object (interval, jitter, max attempts, backoff factor) and have every retry call site read from it. Tests pin that both paths now consult the same source.

You're also tested on **preserving caller ergonomics**: small jobs were happy with the original short call signature. The centralization must not force callers to pass eight new parameters on every invocation. Default arguments or a singleton config make the central source available without burdening callers.

And on **observability survival**: log lines, metrics labels, and audit events that previously named "retry attempt N with M ms backoff" must still produce the same values after centralization, so on-call replays of the outage line up with the new code.

## Good prompts to give your AI

- "Where do retry configurations currently live? Find every assignment of `max_attempts`, `interval_ms`, `jitter_ratio`."
- "If the webhook path uses one config and the inner client uses another, what happens during a retry storm?"
- "What's the smallest change that makes both paths consult the same config without breaking the call signatures of small-job helpers?"
- "Do the log fields / audit envelope keys downstream code depends on still produce the same values?"
- "Is there a sensible default for jitter ratio that lets short calls stay short?"

## Reflexes to fight

- **Refactoring every call site to pass new parameters** — defaults preserve small-job ergonomics
- **Renaming response or audit keys** — these are public contract, leave them
- **Introducing an abstract factory / strategy pattern** — a single dataclass is enough
- **Adding new retry behaviors not in the spec** — exponential backoff, decorrelated jitter, etc. — out of scope
- **Reading config from env vars at call time** — the config is in-process, set once

## Design patterns / concepts this problem maps to

- **Single source of truth**: one config object consulted by every site that needs the values
- **Sensible defaults with override**: short call signatures keep working; longer call signatures override when needed
- **Compose over inherit**: pass the config as a constructor arg, not via subclassing a base class
- **Observability stability**: keys / fields that operators rely on are preserved across the refactor
- **Quiet rejection of bad config**: invalid ratios or negative intervals raise at construction, not at retry time

## When to ask tips-agent for help

| Situation | What to ask |
|---|---|
| About to change call signatures everywhere | "Can defaults preserve the short signature? Use them" |
| Considering env var configuration | "Is config set at startup or at call time?" |
| Adding new retry strategy | "Is exponential backoff in the spec? If no, stay simple" |
| Renaming log keys | "Will operators recognize the new field? Don't break replay" |
| Adding retry to non-retry call sites | "Does every site retry? Don't apply globally if not" |

## Reading the test as the source of truth

The failing tests assert: both retry call sites use the same config object; the audit envelope still carries the same field names; a small-job helper still works without explicit config. These three assertions together pin the centralization scope.

## Self-check before submitting

- Does every retry site consult the same config source?
- Do small-job helpers still work without explicit config parameters?
- Are response / audit keys unchanged from before?
- Did invalid config (negative interval, jitter > 1) raise at construction?
- Did you preserve every public function and every payload key the tests assert on?
- Did you avoid adding new retry strategies beyond what the test exercises?
